lessons.title: Living Organisms and Cell Structure - JAMB Self-Tutoring Lesson
lessons.html:
Living Organisms and Cell Structure

This self-tutoring lesson covers Characteristics of living organisms, cell structure/organelles, and levels of organisation. It follows the JAMB Biology topic structure and is designed so a student can study before attempting the 200-question practice bank.

Learning objectives

  • Explain the main ideas without memorising blindly.
  • Correctly identify and define the key terms used in this topic.
  • Relate each term or process to real farm practice.
  • Distinguish closely related terms from one another.

How to study

  1. Read the explanation slowly.
  2. Write out each key term and its definition in your own words.
  3. Cover the definition and try to recall it from the term alone, then reverse it.
  4. Attempt the practice questions.
  5. Read the explanation even when correct.

Worked example method

Read the question carefully, identify the key term or process being asked about, recall its correct definition or example, eliminate options that describe a different (but related) term, then select the option that matches most precisely.

Common mistakes

  • Confusing two closely related terms (e.g. two similar farming or management systems).
  • Choosing an option that is true in general but does not answer the specific question asked.
  • Overlooking key qualifying words such as 'mainly', 'always' or 'not'.
  • Mixing up crop and animal terminology that sound alike.

Self-test checkpoint

Before continuing, explain the topic in your own words and answer one example without looking at the worked method. If you cannot, return to the explanation and try again.

Worked self-tutoring example

Question: What is the meaning of 'Cell' in Biology (JAMB)?

  1. A. the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms
  2. B. the selectively permeable membrane that encloses the cell and controls what enters and leaves it
  3. C. a fluid-filled sac within a cell used for storage, typically large and permanent in plant cells
  4. D. a characteristic of living organisms involving obtaining and using food for energy and growth

Correct answer: the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms

Step-by-step explanation: 'Cell' means the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

Exam strategy

JAMB Biology questions are largely concept-, structure- and process-based. Build a strong, precise vocabulary for each topic rather than vague general knowledge, since many wrong options are simply the definition of a different (but related) term.

Revision summary

Before moving to the next topic, make sure you can correctly define and give an example for every key term in Living Organisms and Cell Structure without referring back to this lesson.
